vos.title: FBI Says WaterPlum Hackers Drained $10.71M From Bitcoin (BTC) and Crypto Wallets
vos.subTitle:
• The group infected over 30,000 computers across more than 100 countries.
• Data was stolen from more than 7,000 crypto wallets per the joint advisory.
• Japan dismantled its first known laptop farm run by remote North Korean workers.
30,000 Devices, 7,000 Wallets Compromised
A North Korea-linked hacking crew tracked as WaterPlum drained at least $10.71 million in digital assets from crypto users, according to a joint advisory issued Friday by Japan’s National Police Agency (NPA) and the US Federal Bureau of Investigation. The agencies report that WaterPlum — also tracked under the name Contagious Interview — infected more than 30,000 computers across 100-plus countries and exfiltrated data from more than 7,000 crypto wallets, with the wallet cluster receiving the funds between December 2025 and July 2026. The advisory describes a recruitment scam aimed squarely at software builders. Operatives pose as headhunters for artificial-intelligence, crypto and altcoin startups, contacting targets on social media, job boards and freelance marketplaces. Candidates are pushed into a technical interview or coding test and told to download files from code-sharing sites — the excuse being a broken video call or the assignment itself. Those files carry an infostealer that quietly harvests browser passwords, screenshots and keystrokes, and critically extracts the secret keys that control a crypto wallet, the software people use to hold digital money.
Japanese and US authorities say North Korea-linked hackers hit 30,000+ devices and 7,000+ wallets
“WaterPlum actors pose as prospective employers to target software developers and IT professionals worldwide under the pretext of attractive job opportunities,” the joint advisory states. The personas borrow the credibility of the AI boom — a sector where high-profile token ventures such as Worldcoin (WLD) have made constant developer outreach a normal part of hiring. An earlier investigation, in which a researcher spent 22 months inside the group’s servers and mapped 1,640 victims across 57 countries, put the footprint at a fraction of Friday’s official tally, which is roughly 18 times larger. While the advisory does not break the $10.71 million down by asset, funds siphoned in Bitcoin (BTC) and other liquid coins are typically laundered through mixers and cross-chain swaps before reaching final destinations.
Tokyo’s First Laptop Farm Takedown
The dismantling of Japan’s first known laptop farm gives the advisory an operational edge. Investigators say local confidants kept laptops in their own homes while North Korean IT workers abroad controlled the machines remotely, posing as Japanese residents to win freelance contracts. Those workers moved several hundred million yen worth of crypto overseas, and the same internet addresses tied the farm to WaterPlum’s infrastructure. The NPA and FBI assess that WaterPlum cyber actors and some North Korean IT workers operate under the 313 General Bureau of the Munitions Industry Department, subordinate to the Workers’ Party of Korea’s Central Committee — placing the campaign inside the state’s sanctioned revenue apparatus. Analysts have long tied Pyongyang’s crypto theft and proof-of-work mining activity to weapons funding; Friday’s advisory formalizes that chain of command.
The staffing fraud reaches into Japan’s exchange sector. In May 2025, a suspected North Korean operative applied for an engineering role at bitFlyer, a venue covered in our guide to the best crypto exchanges, using a stolen resume. Interviewers flagged several tells: he refused to relocate, demanded payment in crypto and appeared to read answers off a second screen. He was not hired. Earlier campaigns leaned on deepfake recruitment calls to reach senior staff, and the same social-engineering playbook surfaces in retail-facing lures — from passive-income pitches to the mobile-mining narrative that drew users to Pi Network. Investigators now tell engineering teams to run recruiter-submitted code inside a sandbox, a sealed test environment walled off from production files and wallet software.
Endpoint Compromise, Not Protocol Flaws
Read together, the advisory and the laptop-farm takedown describe one machine: a state-run pipeline that converts fake job offers into wallet keys, and wallet keys into hard currency for a sanctioned regime. COINOTAG’s reading of the filing is that the root cause is not a protocol flaw but endpoint compromise — infostealers extracting private keys from developer machines — and the remediation is procedural: sandbox every recruiter artifact, isolate signing keys from daily-use systems, and treat unsolicited hiring tests as hostile code. With $10.71 million confirmed drained and more than 7,000 wallets exposed, the developer community’s threat model must now assume the recruiter is the attack.

vos.title: ZEC’s Rally Is Sending a Bigger Message Than Most Traders Realize
vos.subTitle:
Zcash is doing something the crypto market cannot ignore anymore.

On September 17, ZEC surged roughly 23% in 24 hours to around $1,369, while Bitcoin gained less than 1%. The move pushed Zcash close to $1,400 and dramatically outpaced most major cryptocurrencies.

But focusing only on the percentage gain misses the more interesting story.

ZEC's rally may be telling us something about how this crypto market is changing.

Capital is becoming selective. Older narratives are returning. Privacy is gaining attention again. And traders appear increasingly willing to move toward assets with a specific story rather than simply following Bitcoin.

This Is Bigger Than One Green Candle

A 20% move can happen in crypto without meaning much.

But ZEC's strength didn't begin yesterday.

Zcash was up roughly 168% over the previous 30 days as of September 17, according to CoinGecko data cited by Decrypt. Its market capitalization had climbed to about $22.9 billion.

That makes the move much harder to dismiss as a random one-day pump.

Something has clearly changed in how the market is valuing Zcash.

Price momentum is part of the explanation, but there are deeper forces underneath it.

Privacy Has Become a Narrative Again

For years, privacy coins were pushed to the side while crypto moved toward newer narratives.

DeFi exploded.

NFTs arrived.

Layer 1 networks competed.

Meme coins dominated attention.

AI became another major theme.

Privacy never disappeared, but it stopped being one of the market's loudest stories.

Now that conversation is returning.

Zcash allows users to make shielded transactions that can conceal transaction addresses and amounts while using zero-knowledge proofs to verify transactions.

That feature becomes more interesting as crypto moves closer to mainstream finance.

Public blockchains offer transparency, but complete financial transparency also creates a question the industry increasingly has to answer:

How much financial information should actually be public?

ZEC gives the market a direct way to express that debate.

Big Investors Are Looking Again

The latest rally also received an important boost from institutional attention.

Paradigm co-founder Matt Huang disclosed that the crypto investment firm owns ZEC and described Zcash as a privacy-focused complement to Bitcoin.

That doesn't guarantee ZEC will continue rising.

But it changes the conversation.

For years, many traders treated older cryptocurrencies as projects that had already experienced their best cycles.

Zcash challenges that assumption.

A cryptocurrency doesn't necessarily need to be new to become relevant again.

Sometimes an old technology simply needs the market narrative to catch up with it.

The Network Isn't Standing Still Either

There is another reason this rally deserves attention.

Zcash holders recently participated in a major governance process around the network's upcoming NU7 upgrade.

Nearly 2.4 million ZEC participated in a privacy-preserving coinholder vote. Around 99.9% of participating coins supported reducing target block times from 75 seconds to 25 seconds, while 98.9% supported preserving Zcash's existing Bitcoin-style halving schedule.

Those numbers matter for two different reasons.

Faster blocks could improve how quickly users experience transactions.

Keeping the halving schedule preserves the predictable monetary structure that Zcash shares with Bitcoin.

The proposals still need to move through development and implementation, so a governance vote shouldn't be confused with an already-completed network change.

But the direction is clear.

Zcash isn't simply relying on an old privacy narrative.

Its community is still trying to improve the network.

ZEC Is Also Showing How Rotation Works

There is another message hidden inside the rally.

Bitcoin doesn't need to collapse for another cryptocurrency to dramatically outperform it.

BTC gained less than 1% while ZEC jumped roughly 23% during the same 24-hour period. Solana gained around 3%, while BNB and HYPE rose more than 2%.

That is what selective rotation can look like.

Money doesn't suddenly leave Bitcoin and enter every altcoin equally.

Instead, attention concentrates.

A narrative gains momentum.

Volume follows.

Traders notice the relative strength.

More attention arrives.

And suddenly one corner of the market is moving far faster than everything else.

ZEC may currently be one of the clearest examples of that process.

Old Coins Aren't Necessarily Dead Coins

Crypto traders love new things.

New chains.

New tokens.

New narratives.

New technologies.

Because of that, projects from previous cycles can quickly be labelled irrelevant.

Zcash launched in 2016.

Yet a decade later, it has returned to the center of the market conversation.

That sends a wider message.

The next major crypto narrative doesn't necessarily have to come from something launched yesterday.

If an older project solves a problem that suddenly becomes important again, the market can reprice it very quickly.

Privacy may be one of those problems.

But Momentum Creates Its Own Risk

There is another side to ZEC's extraordinary run.

The stronger the move becomes, the easier it is for traders to confuse a powerful narrative with a price that can only move upward.

Those are different things.

ZEC reached around $1,388 on September 17 after gaining roughly 168% over 30 days.

Moves of that size naturally attract momentum traders and can increase volatility.

A correction would not automatically destroy the privacy narrative.

Likewise, a strong privacy narrative doesn't guarantee that every price level is sustainable.

Separating those two ideas becomes especially important after a rapid rally.

The Bigger Message From ZEC

Maybe Zcash isn't simply telling us something about Zcash.

Maybe it's telling us something about this entire stage of the crypto cycle.

Bitcoin can remain dominant while individual altcoins explode.

Old narratives can become new narratives again.

Institutional attention can return to assets that traders had stopped watching.

And capital can rotate aggressively without creating a traditional market-wide altseason.

That could make this cycle much more selective than previous ones.

Instead of asking when every altcoin will pump, traders may increasingly need to watch where attention, development and liquidity are converging.

Right now, Zcash sits directly in the middle of that conversation.

The price rally is impossible to miss.

But the bigger message may be that privacy  and selective altcoin rotation itself  is becoming relevant again.

vos.title: CFTC Submits Bitcoin (BTC) Market Rules to White House After 49-50 CLARITY Vote
vos.subTitle:
• CFTC submitted crypto market prerule RIN 3038-AF80 to the White House on Sept. 17.
• CFTC no-action letter lets passive wallet software route derivatives orders without broker registration.
• SEC granted qualifying platforms a five-year innovation exemption for tokenized stock trading.
CFTC Draft Reaches OIRA
The Commodity Futures Trading Commission has formally started building a rulebook for digital assets without waiting for Congress, sending a draft regulation on crypto asset transactions and markets to the White House for review on Sept. 17. The action, filed under the title “Regulation Crypto Asset Transactions and Regulation Crypto Asset Markets,” now sits with the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs, the White House office that vets federal rules before they become public. Its prerule designation marks the earliest phase of US rulemaking: no text has been published, so which assets, platforms and intermediaries it would cover remains unknown. The timing is pointed — the submission arrived two days after the Senate failed to advance the CLARITY Act, the market-structure bill that died at 49 votes to 50.
What the Draft May Cover
The official record assigns the filing the code RIN 3038-AF80 and lists it as pending OIRA review, a stage that precedes any formal proposal. Its likely shape can be read from CFTC Chair Michael Selig’s Aug. 20 remarks to the agency’s Innovation Advisory Committee: codify the commission’s view of crypto market structure, and let existing registrants — together with some currently unregistered exchanges — be designated as “crypto asset markets,” a special class of designated contract market where leveraged and margined digital-asset trading could operate under direct CFTC supervision. The draft is also expected to address when retail commodity transactions qualify for the “actual delivery” exemption that permits settlement outside registered venues, a question that shapes how retail-facing platforms among the Best Crypto Exchanges structure their offerings.
Chairs Vow to Press On
Both chairs made clear their agencies will not pause. The day after the vote, Selig wrote on X that the CFTC is “locked in and ready to ship its rules for the new frontier of finance,” while SEC Chair Paul Atkins said the securities regulator would advance “with or without legislation.” Each agency acted the following day — the CFTC with its software relief, the SEC with its tokenized-stock exemptions. Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong added that regulators already hold “the tools they need to create clear rules under existing authority” and predicted they would begin work “in earnest.” In his words, “clarity is coming to crypto regardless” — a view the White House filing now makes concrete.
Relief for Wallet Software
The CFTC paired the filing with immediate relief. A no-action letter published Friday, set out in the agency’s official press release, lets providers of passive software — including crypto wallet apps — connect users to regulated derivatives markets without registering as introducing brokers. Providers may market specific contracts and collect transaction-based fees, but they cannot hold customer assets, generate buy or sell signals of the kind an AI trading bot would produce, or control how orders are routed and executed. The relief carries conditions: risk disclosures, recordkeeping and compliance with marketing rules. It stays in force until the CFTC adopts rules or guidance on registration requirements for software developers.
SEC Opens a Tokenized-Stock Lane
The SEC moved on the same front. On Thursday it issued an “innovation exemption” giving qualifying platforms a five-year conditional path to offer onchain trading of certain tokenized U.S. stocks without registering as national securities exchanges — pulling tokenized equities onto blockchain rails that until now belonged mainly to decentralized finance and Bitcoin DeFi experiments. The step complements the CFTC’s filing rather than competing with it: one builds a derivatives framework, the other opens an equities lane. Hyperliquid Policy Center CEO Jake Chervinsky, responding to the OIRA record, said the CFTC “is moving fast” and appears to have sent a rule proposal into interagency review — an assessment consistent with the filing’s Sept. 17 receipt date.
Prerule, Not Policy — Yet
For COINOTAG’s desk, the prerule is best understood as process, not policy. A prerule is a proposal in gestation: after OIRA finishes its review, the draft returns to the commission for a vote to issue a proposed rule, which then opens a public comment period, and a further vote is required before anything takes effect. Nothing binds exchanges or traders today, and the CFTC has declined to comment on the document’s contents. Still, with the CLARITY Act stalled and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent having previously flagged agency rulemaking as the fallback, this filing is the nearest thing US crypto markets have to a regulatory timeline — and Bitcoin (BTC) and every other asset now await rules that will be written in Washington, not on Capitol Hill.

vos.title: Zcash price enters discovery with $2,000 in sight
vos.subTitle:
Zcash price traded near $1,455 on Sep. 18 after retreating from an intraday high of $1,535, while technical indicators and liquidation data pointed to continued volatility around the $1,500 level.

Zcash price action today

Zcash ( $ZEC ) price rose as high as $1,535.82 before sellers pushed the token back below $1,500, according to the daily chart. ZEC traded at approximately $1,455 at the time of writing, down 0.78% during the current daily session.

The pullback came after an accelerated advance from the $1,100 area. ZEC broke above $1,250 and $1,375 with limited consolidation before testing the $1,500 Murrey Math resistance level.

Price has gained more than 190% since trading near $500 in August. ZEC has also established a sequence of higher highs and higher lows across the daily and 4-hour charts, keeping its wider uptrend intact despite the latest retreat.

The daily Stochastic RSI started recovering from lower levels, with the faster line at 43.69 and the signal line at 30.61. The crossover showed that daily momentum was rebuilding after the indicator cooled during an earlier consolidation.

However, the rejection above $1,500 showed that sellers remained active near the psychological level. ZEC would need a confirmed daily close above that zone to reduce the risk of a deeper pullback.

What is driving the ZEC rally?

The rally followed the Zcash community’s vote on proposals tied to the Network Upgrade 7 roadmap. Nearly 99.9% of participating ZEC reportedly backed reducing the network’s target block time from 75 seconds to 25 seconds, while 98.9% supported keeping its current halving schedule.

The proposed change would shorten transaction confirmation times without increasing daily issuance because the block reward would be adjusted for the faster schedule.

Paradigm co-founder Matt Huang also disclosed the venture firm’s exposure to Zcash in a Sep. 16 post. Huang discussed the network’s development funding and said Paradigm considered the fund important to Zcash’s future.

The disclosure added an institutional element to a rally already supported by the governance vote and renewed interest in privacy-focused cryptocurrencies.

US investors can also access regulated ZEC exposure through Grayscale’s Zcash ETF, which trades on NYSE Arca under the ticker ZCSH. The product gives brokerage customers exposure without requiring them to hold ZEC directly, though its market price can differ from the value of its underlying assets.

Zcash technical indicators remain bullish

The 4-hour chart showed that ZEC’s momentum remained positive even as the token retreated from its latest high.

The moving average convergence divergence indicator stood at 88.30, above its signal line at 76.33. Its positive histogram reading of 11.98 indicated that buyers still controlled the broader momentum trend.

However, the histogram had begun to contract. A continued decline would show that the speed of the rally was slowing, increasing the possibility of consolidation or a short-term correction.

The 4-hour relative strength index stood at 68.35, just below overbought territory. The RSI had also fallen below its moving average at 73.86, showing that short-term buying pressure had eased after the move above $1,500.

ZEC’s immediate resistance sits between $1,500 and the intraday high of $1,535. A 4-hour close above $1,535 could open a move toward the next Murrey Math targets at $1,625 and $1,750.

The first important support lies near $1,420, followed by the former breakout level at $1,375. A close below $1,375 could expose $1,250, which previously acted as a major reversal level.

vos.title: ECB's Lagarde Blocked Binance's MiCA License Bid Over USDT, USDC Stablecoin Concerns
vos.subTitle:
• ECB President Christine Lagarde personally blocked Binance's Greek MiCA license application.
• Binance filed in Greece in January and withdrew its application in mid-June.
• MiCA approval would have given Binance passporting access to 450 million EU residents.
Lagarde's Quiet Veto
European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde personally intervened to stop Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, from winning a Greek license under the EU's bridge protocol-style Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) passporting framework, according to a Wall Street Journal report citing people familiar with the process. Our desk's reading of the reporting is that the intervention was channeled through the government of Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis and arrived at the final stage of a process already trending toward approval. A vice-chair of the Hellenic Capital Market Commission (HCMC) told Binance executives that Lagarde wanted the decision held until the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) takes over exchange licensing under a proposed EU reform that has not been adopted. The timing was striking: in early June, Greek officials had notified ESMA that they were prepared to approve the application, meaning the bid was effectively on its last stretch before being stopped. Binance filed in Greece in January; word of a possible HCMC rejection surfaced in mid-June, when a European crypto-intelligence outlet first reported Lagarde's involvement without authoritative confirmation. Days before MiCA's July 1 effective date, the exchange formally withdrew the filing, forfeiting streamlined access to roughly 450 million EU residents. Under the passporting regime, approval in one member state lets a licensed crypto-asset service provider operate across all 27 — one national review substituting for twenty-seven, the golden ticket for an exchange of Binance's scale. A Binance spokesperson declined to engage with the substance: “We will not comment on speculation.” The same statement stressed that in Europe the exchange remains committed to long-term, compliant operation under MiCA, is actively working toward authorization, and views a license as essential to a consistent, regulated service — vowing to refile in another EU jurisdiction.
The Digital Euro Motive
Why would a central bank lean on an exchange license? The reporting points squarely at stablecoins. Lagarde was reportedly concerned that Binance — whose listings span retail favorites such as Shiba Inu (SHIB) and institutional-grade services alike — could deepen the circulation of dollar-based stablecoins such as USDT and USDC across the EU, undermining the digital euro project and the euro-denominated alternatives meant to challenge it. The concern is structural rather than rhetorical. Dollar-pegged assets dominate stablecoin savings, where decentralized products such as Savings Dai (sDAI) already compete for deposits, and much of that liquidity routes through automated market venues like Curve DAO (CRV). The ECB has repeatedly warned that U.S. dollar stablecoins threaten European monetary sovereignty; handing a giant exchange a regulated distribution channel across the bloc would amplify exactly that exposure. The account adds a second layer of resistance: ESMA privately advised national financial regulators to reject Binance's MiCA applications over the exchange's past compliance record. Binance disputes the premise. Gillian Lynch, its head of Europe, said in early July that the company had met every HCMC requirement: “We were deemed to have a complete application. Nothing was missing, and nothing material was outstanding.” An ECB spokesperson, contacted separately, declined to comment while restating the bank's formal position — it holds no institutional role in authorizing crypto-asset service providers, a competence reserved for national authorities such as the HCMC. The exchange's history frames regulators' caution: founder Changpeng 'CZ' Zhao pleaded guilty in the United States in 2023 to Bank Secrecy Act violations, agreed to $4.3 billion in penalties, served a four-month sentence in 2024, and received a pardon from President Donald Trump in October 2025.
ESMA Consolidation in Play
The legal architecture matters here. MiCA, in force since July 1, empowers national competent authorities — not the ECB — to grant licenses with EU-wide effect, and the ECB's own statement concedes it holds no authorization competence, making Lagarde's leverage political rather than statutory. The reform centralizing licensing at ESMA is still a proposal, not a final rule, so the binding obligations today sit with national regulators and the service providers they license. For Binance, the realistic paths are refiling in another member state — assuming the pressure does not travel — or acquiring an already-licensed European platform.

vos.title: $TAO Is Not an AI Ticker. It Is the Machine Under the Candle.
vos.subTitle:
The market is pricing a red candle. Five companies are pricing the future of intelligence. Only one of those is a trade. OpenAI. Google. Meta. Microsoft. Anthropic. They own the models, the data, the GPUs, and the door you walk through to use any of it. 
That is not an open future. That is a toll road with five owners and no second exit.
Most people still treat $TAO
 like another AI ticker riding a hot narrative. They open the chart, see a token that spent 2026 well below its 2024 high near $758, and ask if they backed the wrong horse.
That is the expensive question.
The cheap question, the one that actually pays, is this. What happens when a network rebuilds the machine under the candle, then makes the machine impossible to capture, while the crowd is still arguing about whether the founder leaving killed the story?
Once you see that gap, you cannot unsee it.
Stop valuing an AI network like a meme $TAO
 is still being priced like a narrative token. It is not.
It is not Airbnb for GPUs. It is not one team wrapping one chatbot and hoping the token stays useful. It is the index for 128 live subnet markets that all settle in and out of TAO. Every subnet that wins has to buy the base asset to exist. Every miner that registers burns TAO. Every emission slice that matters still denominates in TAO.
That is not a side feature. That is the entire economic design.
Bitcoin was money. Ethereum was apps. TAO is intelligence.
If that sentence sounds like branding, look at the category. Bittensor is not competing with other AI coins. It is competing with closed labs for the right to be the infrastructure layer intelligence runs on. Different bet. Different risk. Different payoff if the mechanism holds.
The part the resignation hid
In February 2026 Const and Ala gave up executive titles at the Opentensor Foundation. The timeline read it as the founder walking away.
Wrong frame.
Neither left the work. What got surrendered was the private room that ratifies upgrades. Most chains keep that room filled with friends, employees, or whoever bought the loudest campaign. Bittensor is trying to fill it with whoever the block height points at.
Two houses. Validators in one. Subnet owners in the other. A three seat committee drawn blind from the top of both sets, then rotated every six to eight months. Every objection doubles the delay. The first real use case is starving extractors. Cut emissions to subnets that farm rewards and ship nothing the network wants.
A founder giving up a title is theatre if the same people stay in the room. A lottery that rotates the room is a product.
In a market that pays whoever produces the most useful intelligence, being impossible to capture is not a feature. It is the thing serious capital was waiting to see before it sizes in.
The chart will be the last place this shows up.
The rebuild almost nobody priced
While holders stared at $220, the rules that decide who earns changed.
The first halving already hit. December 2025. Daily issuance dropped from roughly 7,200 TAO to 3,600. Hard cap still 21 million. No premine. No VC carve out. Fair launch scarcity applied to an AI commodity instead of a hash commodity.
dTAO turned every subnet into a tiny economy. Each one has an alpha token that trades against TAO. The smoothed alpha price feeds emissions. Strong markets pull more of the 3,600. Weak ones hit the emission gate and get throttled. The market, not a committee chat, decides where the reward pool goes.
Root Reborn killed a silent leak. Nearly half of TAO sits on root. Alpha dividends used to sell into TAO automatically, every day, whether anyone wanted the sale or not. Now they accrue in validator linked baskets and only convert when someone claims. Mechanical sell pressure got dialled down. That is plumbing. Plumbing is how networks survive.
Growth now tightens supply. Neuron registration burns TAO through dynamic pricing. New subnets cost TAO. Owners can burn alpha. Three contraction mechanisms run at once, and they accelerate if the network actually grows. Most tokens have one burn gimmick. TAO has a system where demand structurally requires scarcity.
128 markets. About 25 will matter.
Think of TAO as the S&P 500 of decentralised AI. Each subnet is a stock competing for emissions. The index sits in the pool opposite every alpha token, so when a subnet wins, TAO wins with it.
Around 100 of those markets will never matter. The other 25 are the entire reason the token exists. Most people cannot tell them apart. The market eventually will.
The filter is not cool repo. Dynamic TAO turned every subnet into an investment vehicle overnight. Emissions are not revenue. Usage tweets are not invoices. Alpha market cap is not audited business value. A category can print a billion dollars of quoted subnet value and still have thin exits and no outside customers.
Watch the names that already look like companies, not contests.
Chutes, SN64. Inference at scale, the subnet that keeps showing up wherever developers actually pay for tokens out.
Targon, SN4. Compute and confidential hardware, the privacy wall.
Score, SN44. Computer vision leaving the terminal and walking into physical sites.
Templar, SN3. Permissionless pre training in public, the Bitcoin of AI thesis running live instead of sitting in a thread.
Ridges and the coding markets. The ones that have to beat funded labs on engineering benchmarks, not vibes.
If a subnet cannot explain the difference between runway and revenue, it is dead weight wearing a whitepaper.
What the smartest capital already did
Barry Silbert did not sprinkle TAO into a basket. Through DCG he stood up Yuma, a company whose job is to accelerate and finance the Bittensor stack. That is a statement, not a trade.
Stillcore, with Jason Calacanis in the mix, framed 2026 TAO against ETH in 2016 and BTC in 2013, and set out to own a real slice of supply plus the highest conviction subnets. Mark Jeffrey called it a foundational layer. Grayscale ran the old playbook. Fund first, trust second, ETF paperwork after that. Polychain was early. Jensen Huang talking about decentralised training did not create the network. It told the last group of skeptics the architecture was no longer a crypto in joke.
None of that is a guarantee. All of it is the opposite of nobody serious is here.
The people with the best track records are not scrolling past the ticker. They are building permanent vehicles around one network while the timeline debates a daily candle.
The only number the chain still cannot show you
Bittensor is gorgeous onchain. Stake, emissions, pools, alpha prices, validator weight. You can audit the internal economy in real time.
It cannot yet hand you a complete, audited ledger of customer cash arriving from outside the loop. AI requests and commercial contracts still live off chain. Token throughput is not a receipt. Partnerships are not margins. A widely circulated 43 million dollar Q1 revenue line should stay in the rumor pile until it can be checked.
That is not a reason to leave. It is the reason to watch the right variable.
Price tells you how the crowd feels. Six signals tell you whether emissions are becoming a business.
Does TAO hold gains while 3,600 new tokens still hit the market every day.
Do subnet gains broaden, or is it five names with everyone else illiquid.
When does custom root weight setting actually go live.
Which subnets lose share under the emission gate.
Independent proof of customer payments and margins. Cash. Not tokens processed.
ETF status as a stage, not a vibe. Filing, amendment, effectiveness, launch. Do not mix them up.
A subnet can look rich in alpha and still bleed you against TAO. The risk sits one layer deeper than the price might fall.
The hook you should keep
Five companies own the toll road.
Bittensor is trying to be the alternative route. Open markets for intelligence, Yuma Consensus scoring work no other chain can score, 21 million hard cap, post halving issuance already cut in half, 128 competing subnets, two voting houses, a committee the chain picks and then fires.
The network always leads. The price always follows. It just runs late.
You do not learn $TAO  by watching $TAO
. You learn it by reading the mechanism, then checking whether the 25 subnets that matter are turning emissions into invoices.
The people who read the docs always buy before the people who read the price.
The candle is weather.
The machine is the trade.
Explainer, not advice. Figures move. Verify subnets on Taostats, read filings as filings, and never size a position off a hook, even this one.

vos.title: NYSE Tested Avalanche (AVAX) Technology for a Year, Ava Labs President Says
vos.subTitle:
• NYSE spent roughly a year testing Avalanche technology, Ava Labs President Charley Cooper said.
• ICE executive Michael Blaugrund said Avalanche checks many of its infrastructure requirements.
• Ava Labs confirmed NYSE has not yet selected a blockchain for its tokenized securities platform.
NYSE's Year of Testing Avalanche
The New York Stock Exchange has spent roughly a year testing Avalanche (AVAX) technology while it builds infrastructure for tokenized U.S. stocks and ETFs, Ava Labs President Charley Cooper said on Thursday. Cooper made the disclosure during an appearance at the Avalanche Summit in New York, explaining that NYSE examined both the technical performance of the network and the economics behind it as it weighed how the chain could fit into existing market systems. “They weren’t just kicking the tires on our technology,” Cooper said. “They wanted to make sure that we understood their business and their economics.” He described what he called a close working relationship between Ava Labs and NYSE while declining to claim a victory: “I leave it to the NYSE guys to talk publicly about where they are in the whole process.” Appearing alongside him, Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) Head of Strategic Initiatives Michael Blaugrund said the NYSE parent has remained “very engaged” with the Avalanche team while evaluating blockchain networks, and that “Avalanche checks a lot of those boxes” for its requirements. NYSE has not publicly named the chain or chains that would power its planned digital securities venue, and the proposed architecture is deliberately built to accommodate multiple networks for settlement and custody. The exchange first disclosed its digital trading platform plans in January, and NYSE President Lynn Martin said in August that work on onchain settlement infrastructure was continuing. The venue pairs NYSE’s Pillar matching engine with blockchain-based post-trade infrastructure and, pending regulatory approval, would support tokenized versions of listed securities alongside natively issued onchain assets, with continuous trading, immediate settlement, fractional shares, dollar-denominated orders and stablecoin-based funding; tokenized shareholders would keep conventional rights, including dividends and governance. To assemble the stack, ICE agreed late August to invest in tZERO and license its blockchain patents, building on a March memorandum with Securitize, NYSE’s first named digital transfer agent. COINOTAG’s Avalanche desk has tracked the buildout through 2026.
SEC Exemption and the 24-Hour ATS
The executive’s remarks circulated through Avalanche’s official X account on September 17, and they sit inside a larger ICE project: an alternative trading system, a regulated venue separate from the main exchange, designed to let stocks and ETFs trade as tokens around the clock. Blaugrund said in January that building market infrastructure for onchain trading, settlement, custody and funding is a strategic priority for ICE, so the ATS itself is not new — what is new is the public naming of Avalanche as a leading candidate. His comments mark an evaluation stage only: neither ICE nor NYSE has announced a formal contract or an adoption decision. The regulatory backdrop shifted this week, when the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission granted eligible venues conditional five-year relief to trade tokenized National Market System stocks through permissioned automated market maker pools, with conditions covering shareholder rights, smart contracts, trading limits and coordinated market halts. Cooper expects some trading venues to begin offering 24-hour weekday access within the next year, though he stopped short of predicting that the largest exchanges — the LSEs, the NYSEs, the CMEs — will move on the same timetable, noting that smaller venues competing for liquidity could act faster. The ecosystem context reinforces the momentum. In July, Japanese tokenization platform Progmat migrated every active security token project it manages, representing more than ¥452 billion in underlying assets, from Corda 5 to a dedicated Avalanche Layer 1 with Ethereum Virtual Machine compatibility. South Korea’s Hanwha Investment & Securities has completed a tokenized securities platform supporting Avalanche and Hyperledger Besu ahead of the country’s regulated framework for blockchain securities arriving in February 2027, as we covered in Hanwha Securities to Tokenize Stocks and Bonds on Avalanche (AVAX). Institutional reach is broadening into brokerage too, with Charles Schwab set to add the asset to its 39.9-million-account platform per Charles Schwab to Add Avalanche (AVAX) to Schwab Crypto’s 39.9M-Account Platform — a pipeline where tokenized shares would ultimately function like any other dapp on the network.
Tokenized Equities Race Takes Shape
The two threads form a single arc: a year of due diligence at the world’s largest securities market, now paired with a regulator that has cleared a legal route for permissioned tokenized stock trading. The most load-bearing primary record this week remains the official Avalanche post carrying Blaugrund’s remarks — it confirms ICE’s engagement with the network but also its limits, because what was disclosed is an evaluation, not a signed selection, with no launch date and no disclosed investment size. Our reading is that NYSE’s testing amounts to technological validation of the Avalanche stack, and with the SEC’s five-year exemption in place, the network now sits credibly inside the shortlist for a round-the-clock U.S. equities market. Institutional demand is pulling large-cap altcoin attention toward tokenization plays, and markets have started pricing that in: AVAX spot gained 6.8% over the past 24 hours.

vos.title: Hyperliquid (HYPE) Tops $90 for the First Time After 15% Two-Day Rally
vos.subTitle:
• Hyperliquid's manual borrowing service drew $269 million in assets on its first day.
• The SEC issued a five-year innovation exemption for tokenized stock platforms on September 17.
• Aksel Kibar set a $100.5 chart target for HYPE with $76.6 as key defense.
HYPE Crosses $90 for the First Time
Hyperliquid (HYPE) crossed the $90 threshold for the first time on Thursday, capping a two-day advance of more than 15% that has lifted the token's year-to-date return past 250%. Live pricing shows HYPE, the native asset of the decentralized exchange Hyperliquid, changing hands at $91.99, up 12.49% over the past 24 hours — and our read of the order flow points to a steady stair-step of buy pressure rather than a single liquidation-driven spike. Three catalysts landed inside roughly 48 hours. The protocol's official announcement confirms manual borrowing went live on its HyperCore layer, with about $269 million in assets borrowed on day one — a figure that matters because holders can now post HYPE or Bitcoin as collateral and draw USDC or USDT without selling their spot positions. At the same time, the SEC issued a temporary five-year exemption for tokenized stock trading venues, and two outside venues — NEAR and Payward, Kraken's parent company — committed to routing derivatives activity through the platform. Each leg removes a distinct constraint on demand: capital efficiency for long-term holders, regulatory headroom for tokenized equities, and distribution through external interfaces — a structural repricing for DeFi infrastructure more broadly. For traders sizing entries around the move, our guide on how to trade on Hyperliquid walks through the venue's mechanics end to end.
Top-10 Entry and a $100.5 Chart Target
The rally carried HYPE into the top 10 cryptocurrencies by market capitalization, displacing Dogecoin from the tenth slot. The token printed an all-time high just under $90 before entering price discovery, the zone above prior resistance where few resting sell orders remain. Trading volume exceeded $1.58 billion around the record, with market capitalization near $22.6 billion at that moment. Momentum screens corroborate the move: Kyle Doops' relative-strength screen cleared just 3 top-20 altcoins, led by HYPE. On the chart, technical analyst Aksel Kibar of Tech Charts read the daily candlestick pattern as a completed breakout, pullback and continuation sequence, projecting a medium-term target of $100.5, with $76.6 — the level that previously acted as strong resistance — the line buyers must hold. The structural bid underneath is the chain's deflationary design: nearly 99% of all trading fees generated on the exchange are automatically spent buying HYPE back from the open market and burning it. That sink converts venue activity directly into scarcity, a mechanism that compounds as derivatives volume on the platform grows.
SEC Exemption and Widening Distribution
The regulatory leg arrived on September 17, when the SEC issued an order it labeled the 'innovation exemption.' The measure grants tokenized securities trading platforms conditional, five-year relief under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, permitting licensed market makers and liquidity aggregators to trade tokenized shares of the national market system on public blockchains. The scope is narrower than the headline suggests: only tokenized common stock carrying genuine shareholder rights — dividends and voting — qualifies, while synthetic products, including tokenized securities swaps, remain excluded. Hyperliquid sits squarely in that corridor because its HIP-3 framework lets developers stake HYPE to deploy their own perpetual markets on the platform's order book; the venue trade.xyz has already used it to list tokenized stock perps. Real-world-asset markets made up roughly 2% of the protocol's total volume in January and now account for about half. Distribution widened in parallel. The Hyperliquid ecosystem now backstops NEAR's default perpetuals interface, supplying the order book, matching engine, more than 50 markets and leverage up to 40x, while NEAR's front end lets users trade assets spread across more than 30 chains. And on September 16, Kraken parent Payward said it intends to bring blockchain-based perpetual futures to its US customers through Hyperliquid and HIP-3 markets, pending regulatory approvals.
$92.74 Is the Level That Matters Now
COINOTAG's proprietary 42-indicator composite S/R scoring engine rates the $92.74 resistance at 73/100 (STRONG), driven by a Keltner Upper and Donchian Upper confluence plus a fresh MACD cross — making it the first ceiling above the $91.99 spot print. The nearest floor is $87.09, scored 67/100 on Ichimoku Tenkan and Kijun agreement, with $75.14 (62/100, SMA 50 and Fibo 0.500) stacked behind it. Derivatives positioning reads constructive but not overheated: funding at 0.0058% and $2.29 billion in open interest show leveraged longs building steadily, while RSI at 66.11 and a Fear & Greed reading of 56/100 (Greed) support the uptrend, despite the engine's bearish MACD signal flagging short-term exhaustion risk. A daily close below $87.09 would invalidate the continuation thesis; a confirmed break of $92.74 reopens the path toward $103.

vos.title: 🐕 $62M+ in Shiba Inu Futures Positions Remain Open as Traders Face Liquidation Risk
vos.subTitle:
🐕 $62M+ in Shiba Inu Futures Positions Remain Open as Traders Face Liquidation Risk

Shiba Inu (SHIB) traders continue to hold more than $62 million in open futures positions, keeping leverage firmly in focus as derivatives activity remains significantly larger than spot trading.

According to CoinGlass data, SHIB’s open interest recently stood around $62.25 million, while 24-hour futures trading volume reached approximately $54.42 million. Open interest represents futures positions that remain open, meaning a substantial amount of leveraged exposure is still active in the market. (thecryptobasic.com)

📊 Futures Activity Dominates

The difference between futures and spot activity is notable.

Recent data showed roughly $54.25 million in SHIB futures volume compared with around $19.99 million in spot volume over 24 hours. That means futures trading was approximately 2.7× the spot volume during the period.

This doesn’t automatically indicate whether traders are bullish or bearish. Instead, it shows that derivatives are playing a major role in SHIB’s current market activity. (thecryptobasic.com)

⚠️ Liquidations Are Already Happening

The elevated futures exposure comes with increased liquidation risk.

CoinGlass data reported approximately $182,650 in SHIB futures liquidations over 24 hours, involving 73 traders. Long positions represented roughly $162,740, while short positions accounted for about $19,910. (thecryptobasic.com)

This means bullish leveraged traders experienced the majority of the reported liquidations during that period.

📈 SHIB Rebounds, But Leverage Remains

SHIB recently experienced a short-term rebound, trading around the $0.0000050 area in the reported period. However, the token remained below its weekly high near $0.0000054.

The combination of a price rebound and elevated open interest is worth watching because leveraged positions can amplify price movements in either direction.

If SHIB continues higher, short positions could potentially face increasing pressure.

If SHIB reverses lower, highly leveraged long positions could face additional liquidations.

🐋 Exchange Outflows Add Another Factor

CryptoQuant data also showed approximately 249.4 billion SHIB leaving centralized exchanges, while exchange reserves remained above 87 trillion SHIB.

Exchange outflows can reduce the amount of tokens immediately available for trading on centralized exchanges, although an outflow by itself does not guarantee that selling pressure will decrease or that price will rise. (디지털투데이 (DigitalToday))

🔥 SHIB Burn Activity Rises

SHIB’s burn activity also increased during the same period.

Around 27.36 million SHIB were reportedly burned over 24 hours, with the daily burn rate increasing sharply. Weekly burns were reported at approximately 118 million SHIB. (디지털투데이 (DigitalToday))

Burns permanently remove tokens from circulation, but the effect on price depends on the scale of burns relative to SHIB’s enormous circulating supply.

👀 What Traders Are Watching

vos.title: BITCOIN JUST BROKE OUT OF THE FEAR ZONE
vos.subTitle:
This is the kind of move that makes me pay attention.

A few days ago, Bitcoin was trading near $75K after the CLARITY Act failed in the Senate and the Fed delivered its first rate hike since 2023. Today, BTC has pushed back toward $81K, while SOL has climbed above $110 and the altcoin market has moved back above $220B.

What changed?

The market realized that the regulatory story did not end with CLARITY.

The CFTC has now sent its proposed crypto market rules to the White House for review, moving ahead with rulemaking even after the Senate setback. The SEC has also introduced a five-year exemption framework for platforms trading tokenized stocks on blockchain, while requiring those tokens to carry the same shareholder rights as the underlying stocks.

That is a pretty important distinction.

I was watching the CLARITY vote because legislation can create a much cleaner framework. But the market is now getting something else: regulators are continuing to build the framework themselves.

At the same time, Bitcoin is showing me something technically interesting.

BTC went from roughly $75K to above $80K in just a few sessions. The latest move is not happening in isolation either. Solana is back above $106, total crypto market cap is around $2.66T, and several large-cap altcoins are outperforming Bitcoin on the rebound.

For me, $82K is now the level I care about.

That area has repeatedly acted as the upper edge of Bitcoin’s recent range. A clean break above it would tell me the market is finally trying to move beyond the range that has capped BTC for weeks. Until then, I see this as a strong recovery, but not something I want to chase blindly.

There is also a macro contradiction here that I find fascinating.

The Fed just raised rates to 3.75%-4.00%, and the 10-year Treasury yield remains close to 5%. On paper, that is not the environment where I would expect crypto to suddenly rip higher. Yet Bitcoin is doing exactly that.

That tells me crypto is currently responding to more than just interest rates.

Regulation, liquidity expectations, positioning and risk appetite are all fighting for control of the tape.

So I’m not calling this a new bull run yet.

I’m watching $82K on Bitcoin, $110 on SOL, and whether altcoins can keep gaining without BTC dominance ripping higher again.

If those pieces continue to line up, this rebound gets a lot more interesting.
